questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II & III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some doctors are tigers.

All tigers are umbrellas.

Some umbrellas are buses.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some doctors are umbrellas.

II. Some tigers are umbrellas.

III. Some buses are umbrellas.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58da579dd09a905a08a7fa55f08d73622c6e8f290af7281be9aec715f50c412a.png]

I. Some doctors are umbrellas. → **Follows** (As, Some doctors are tigers and All tigers are umbrellas)

II. Some tigers are umbrellas. → Follows (As, All tigers are umbrellas)

III. Some buses are umbrellas. → Follows (As, Some umbrellas are buses)

Hence, '**All conclusions follow**' is the correct answer.

questions.question: It connects all types of computers across the world. Which communication technology is being spoken about here?

• It connects **computers, servers, routers,** and other devices across the world.
 
• Internet uses various communication protocols such as** TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, SMTP,** etc. to ensure **seamless data transfer** between different types of computers and networks.
 
• With the help of Internet, users can access a wide range of **services and applications** such as **email, social media, online shopping, video conferencing, cloud computing**, and much more.
 
• Internet has revolutionized the way people **communicate, work, learn, and entertain** themselves.
 
• It has become an** integral part **of our daily lives.

• It was popular in the **1990s** but has become obsolete with the advent of smartphones and mobile internet.
 
 
 
• **Post cards **are a form of **traditional mail **that carries a **short message or image **on a small piece of paper or cardboard.
 
 
• They are still used for **personal and business correspondence**, but their usage has declined due to the rise of email and instant messaging.
 
 
 
• **Cable** refers to a **physical medium of transmitting data and signals,** such as coaxial cable, fiber optic cable, or Ethernet cable.
 
 
• It is used in various communication technologies such as** cable TV, broadband internet, and LAN** (Local Area Network).

questions.question: After the passage of which Constitutional Amendment Act, are there now six fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment in 1978.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** is the Constitutional Amendment Act that reduced the number of fundamental rights from seven to six by removing the right to property as a fundamental right.
 
• **102nd Amendment in 1996** was related to the implementation of the **Mandal Commission report** on reservations in jobs and education for **Other Backward Classes (OBCs).**
 
• 44th Amendment in 1952 **does not exist** as the Constitution of India was adopted in 1950 and the first amendment was made in 1951.
 
• 11th Amendment in 1952 **does not exist** as there were only three amendments made in 1951, which were related to the salaries of the President, Vice-President, and Governors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental rights** are a set of basic rights that are guaranteed to all citizens under the Constitution of India.
 
• These include the** right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, freedom of religion, right to life and liberty,** and** cultural and educational rights.**
 
• The **Right to Education **was added as the** sixth fundamental right** by the** 44th Amendment in 1978**, which made it the responsibility of the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
• The **Right to Education** was further strengthened by the** 86th Amendment in 2002**, which made education a fundamental right for children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
 
• This amendment also made it mandatory for private schools to **reserve 25% of their seats** for children from economically weaker sections.

questions.question: Which of the following Metals of Harappan civilization got from present-day Rajasthan and Oman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper** was one of the** main metals **used by the **Harappan civilization,** and they sourced it from present-day **Rajasthan and Oman**.
 
• The Harappans used copper for various purposes, including making** tools, weapons, and ornaments.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tin:**

 
 
• While tin was not sourced from Rajasthan or Oman, it was an **important metal **for the Harappans.
 
• They used it to make** bronze,** which is an alloy of copper and tin.
 
• Bronze was used to make a variety of objects, including** tools, weapons, and statues.**
 
 
 
• **Gold and silver:**
 
 
• These precious metals were **not as common** as copper and tin in Harappan society.
 
• Gold was likely used for **jewelry and decorative objects**, while silver may have been used as a form of currency.
 
• The Harappans were skilled at working with these metals and produced** intricate jewelry **and other objects using techniques such as filigree and granulation.

questions.question: Pinky fills her car tank with 20 liters of petrol. She goes on a journey and end up with just 5.5 liters of petrol left in the tank. What is the percent change in the petrol in the tank?

Change in quantity = Initial − Final = 20 − 5.5 = 14.5 liters.

Percent change = (Change ÷ Initial base) × 100

⇒ Percent change = (14.5 ÷ 20) × 100

⇒ Percent change = 14.5 × 5 = 72.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 72.5%.**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Change in petrol = Initial amount − Final amount

⇒ Change = 20 − 5.5 = 14.5 liters

⇒ Percentage Change = (Change ÷ Initial amount) × 100

⇒ Percentage Change = (14.5 ÷ 20) × 100

⇒ Percentage Change = 14.5 × 5

Percentage Change

Percentage change indicates the degree of change over time, relative to the initial value. Formula: % Change = (New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value × 100.

Base Value in Percentage

Always calculate the percentage increase or decrease on the initial (old) value unless specifically mentioned otherwise in the question.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed successively by a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by: (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: On 10 February 2014, a train leaves Delhi at 6 a.m. and reaches Jainagar at 10 a.m.. Another train leaves Jainagar at 8 a.m. and reaches Delhi at 11:30 a.m.. At what time do the two trains cross each other?

Distance covered by 1st train in 2 hrs (6:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m.) = 7 × 2 = 14 units.

Remaining distance = 28 − 14 = 14 units.

Time to cross after 8:00 a.m. = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 14 ÷ (7 + 8) = 14/15 hours = 56 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 8:56 a.m.**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time to meet = Remaining Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by Train 1 = 10:00 a.m. − 6:00 a.m. = 4 hours.

⇒ Time taken by Train 2 = 11:30 a.m. − 8:00 a.m. = 3.5 hours = 7/2 hours.

⇒ Speed of Train 1 = D/4

⇒ Convert 14/15 hours into minutes: 14/15 × 60 = 56 minutes.

⇒ Discount given = 6% of 112 = (6 × 112) ÷ 100 = 6.72

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 112 − 6.72 = 105.28

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 105.28 − 100 = 5.28

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (5.28 ÷ 100) × 100 = 5.28%

Successive Percentage Formula

Relation between CP, MP, and SP

The Marked Price is always calculated by increasing the Cost Price by the given markup percentage. A discount is then applied exclusively on the Marked Price to deduce the Selling Price.

Profit or loss is strictly evaluated on the base Cost Price. The formula is Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. If SP > CP, the difference indicates a profit; otherwise, it is a loss.
